hook.line: Before you ask about money, family or a mistake, Colombians often ask permission to ask. Nobody says no. It is a courtesy pause, a breath before the hard part.
hook.en: Can I ask you a question? (to a friend)

rule:
Before something delicate, ask for the right to ask. With friends: *¿Puedo hacerte una pregunta?* or *¿Te puedo decir una cosa?* The *te* goes before *puedo* or on the end of the infinitive.

With someone you call *usted*, step up: *¿Me permite un comentario?* or *¿Podría preguntarle…?*

Add *un poco personal* as a warning, or *¿Me aceptas un consejo?* before advice. Then ask.
smallPrint: Teachers call this a pre-sequence: a short question that prepares the real one.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *hacerte* or *hacerme*, then type the whole sentence to a friend: Can I ask you a question? *¿Puedo ___ una pregunta?*
yourTurn.why: *Te* means you, and it sticks to the end of the infinitive.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: Can I tell you something?
yourTurn.why: *Te* can go before *puedo* or on the end of *decir*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to someone you call *usted*: May I make a comment?
yourTurn.why: *Permite* is the polite, *usted* way to ask for the floor.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: Can I ask you a slightly personal question?
yourTurn.answer: ¿Puedo hacerte una pregunta un poco personal?
accept: ¿Te puedo hacer una pregunta un poco personal?
yourTurn.why: *Un poco personal* warns the other person before you ask.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it formal. *¿Puedo preguntarte por qué cambiaste de opinión?* Say, to someone you call *usted*: Could I ask you why you changed your mind?
yourTurn.answer: ¿Podría preguntarle por qué cambió de opinión?
yourTurn.why: For *usted*, use *podría* and *le*, and the *usted* verb *cambió*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it plural. *¿Puedo hacerte una pregunta?* Say: Can I ask you all a question?
yourTurn.why: *Les* is the *you all* word, in place of *te*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: Would you accept some advice from me?
yourTurn.why: Ask before you advise: the friend can then say yes or brace themselves.

pitfalls.why: Almost. *Te* attaches to the end of the infinitive as one word: *hacerte*.
Almost. In Spanish you *hacer* a question, and *preguntar* is for the thing you want to know.
Almost. *Te* is for friends; with someone you call *usted*, switch to *le* and the softer *podría*.
